runs.scope: First full pipeline run — treating all history through v0.2.0 as the scanned range (no prior Git tags exist)
runs.notes: Repo's tracked docs are all <=13 days old (post-v0.2.0 release on 2026-03-31), so no staleness remediation was needed. Untracked files (skills/ and docs/tech-writing-adaptation-plan.md) were excluded from freshness scan because the scanner reads git log timestamps — they will be picked up on the next run after commit. Only 4 commits exist in git history, none using conventional-commit format, so changelog categorization was done by reading the v0.2.0 release body.

runs.scope: Second run after committing the tech-writing skill suite under tag v0.2.0. Scan window: since v0.2.0 tag.
runs.notes: Added an [Unreleased] section to CHANGELOG.md covering commit c41aa41 (tech-writing skill suite). No release notes drafted (no new version cut). Both possibly_stale flags (agent_execution_flow.md, llm_tool_call_compatibility.md) are false positives: the scanner treated the new commit as a 'related code change' because it touched repo-root-adjacent paths, but the commit only added files under skills/ and docs/ — nothing that invalidates those two design docs. This is a finding worth feeding back into the freshness scanner's heuristic (Phase 2 improvement: filter 'related changes' by path overlap with the doc's referenced modules rather than any commit touching the repo).

runs.scope: Verification run after landing the path-overlap relevance fix (Phase 2 item 1). Same scan window as run #2.
runs.notes: Both previously-flagged false positives (agent_execution_flow.md, llm_tool_call_compatibility.md) now correctly classify as fresh. The commits that remain in their 'related_code_changes' lists are legitimate — they touch files the docs explicitly name (core/memento_s/agent.py, middleware/llm/llm_client.py). The meta-commit c41aa41 no longer appears in any doc's related list. 17/17 unit tests pass (skills/doc-freshness/scripts/test_relevance.py). Design note: docs/design/doc-freshness-relevance-filter.md.

runs.scope: Run after landing Phase 2 items 2 and 3 in a single pass: --include-untracked flag on doc-freshness, plus style guide Rules 3.6 (no trailing colons on headings) and 9.1 (MDX front matter). Scanned with --include-untracked enabled to exercise the new code path.
runs.notes: All 11 docs classified fresh (3 new docs surfaced via --include-untracked: docs/api/skill-gateway.md, docs/design/doc-freshness-relevance-filter.md, docs/phase-1-retrospective.md — all now tracked after subsequent commits). 20/20 unit tests pass, including 3 new integration tests that spin up a temp git repo to verify the --include-untracked toggle. Phase 2 candidates 1, 2, and 3 from docs/phase-1-retrospective.md are now complete.

runs.scope: Phase 2 item #4 — style-checker auto-fix script. Converts the interactive, agent-driven style checker into a deterministic CLI linter suitable for pre-commit hooks and CI. Implements the six mechanical rules (3.1 sentence case, 3.2 heading-level jumps, 3.6 trailing colons, 4.1 fence language tags, 6.1 blank line before lists, 7.1 descriptive link text — report-only).
runs.notes: Design spec MS-DES-0002 landed first (docs-first mentality honored). Script is stdlib-only, Python 3.10+, ~600 lines with inline commentary; test suite is 34 plain-assert tests (no pytest dependency), all passing. Idempotence verified: second-pass run on the 6 authored docs reports 'checked 6 files: clean'. Fence-aware and MDX front-matter-aware — content inside code fences and YAML front matter is passed through verbatim. Rule 7.1 is report-only (link-text rewriting needs context the script doesn't have). 156 findings on legacy pre-style-guide docs (AUTO_UPDATE_README.md, CHANGELOG_bounded_context_merge.md, UPDATE_SUMMARY.md, agent_execution_flow.md, llm_tool_call_compatibility.md, and CJK-content files) were intentionally left unfixed — those predate the style guide and belong to a separate baseline-cleanup task, not this feature. Phase 2 candidates 1–4 complete; remaining open items from the retrospective: #5 (doc-generator translation/localization pass) and #6 (BM25 retrieval layer for skill search).
